rationale: A Parkinson CBD comparison used corn oil in both arms and measured Epworth sleepiness. The linked results from another registered corn-oil comparator were retracted. An esterified corn-oil study gives a correlation with omega-3 status. No qualifying refined-corn-oil effect is isolated. A later review reports inconclusive Epworth means for omega-3 versus the corn ester group. The full original does not yet verify arm values, sample denominator and time point.

The oil add-on and oil-coupled ultrasound provide indirect pelvic-pain estimates, while the menopause joint-pain comparison was inconclusive. A recovered cancer-treatment trial reports improved aggregate oral symptoms after topical cold-pressed oil plus Solcoseryl. The pain item was unreported. The frozen Parkinson pain direction remains unresolved. The exact publisher and PDF locators are confirmed. The accessible original abstract reports a pain-domain advantage but no magnitude, verified processing grade or Parkinson comparison.

One single-blind oral flaxseed-oil osteoarthritis trial (DOI10.36347/sjams.2019.v07i09.031) and a potentially overlapping rheumatoid-arthritis report from the same investigators (Vyas 2020, independence uncertain) report lower rest and movement arthritis pain, though pressing grade is unreported and dosing/numeric reporting is inconsistent. Competing trials show null pain contrasts for flaxseed versus corn oil after ACL surgery (p=.96), versus linoleic acid in rheumatoid arthritis (n=22), and versus vitamin E in cyclic mastalgia (p=.142), while Parkinson flaxseed-omega-3 plus vitamin-E trials omit pain items. The single-blind oral arthritis pain comparison retains only a minimal_signal easing lean. A separate endometriosis trial reports favorable flax-versus-placebo pain estimates. Its original and protocol conflict on formulation and do not verify a cold-pressed oil. The additional finding does not change the existing ordinal tier.
